SKIN. [46] [Coloc.]
Dryness and heat of skin.
Itching : prickling ; crawling ; formication.
Burning, jerking, tearing pain.
Smarting, itching, followed by perspiration.
Herpes (scabby) on face.
Itch-like eruptions.
Itching, burning ulcers.
Carbuncles, with continuous burning pain.
Boils on neck and face.
Desquamation over whole body.
Corns.
   

STAGE OF LIFE, CONSTITUTION. [47] [Coloc.]
Blonde persons.
Persons subject to violent attacks of cramp colic from fruit, lead poisoning or excessive venery.
Rheumatic or gouty rheumatic diathesis.
Neuralgia of the small branches of the infraorbital nerves, in plethoric, choleric, irritable men, from 40 to 50 years of age, and disposed to hemorrhoidal and gouty affections and to congestions towards head ; most frequent cause was vexation, but sometimes too close application to business ; but once produced, this neuralgia was apt to recur many days successively at same hour, in forenoon.
Boy, æt. 4, feeble constitution, suffering frequently from constipation ; paralysis of rectum.
Boy, æt. 13 ; violent headache for ninety hours.
Boy, æt. 13, after catching cold ; rheumatism.
Minna G., æt. 17, had begun to menstruate ; ischias.
A young countryman, æt. 18, had suffered for several weeks ; rheumatic sciatica.
Servant girl, æt. about 23, healthy complexion, intelligent appearance ; neuralgia of left face.
Miss W. B., æt. about 20, after taking cold ; acute gastritis.
Miss C., æt. 23 ; dysentery.
Mrs. L., æt. 24, fond of tea and coffee, of a venous, hemorrhoidal temperament, yellow complexion, inclined to hysterical affections, subject to cramps in stomach and pain in back, and suffering under stoppage of menses ; neuralgia of solar plexus.
Young woman, æt. 25, suffering for five years ; ovarian tumor.
Girl, æt. 26 ; scrofulous during childhood, not well developed ; headache.
Woman, æt. 26, in sixth week of lactation, in consequence of catching cold ; colic.
Man, æt. 27 ; ischias.
Woman, æt. 27, with amenorrhœa and chronic disposition to vomit ; faceache.
ME., æt. 28 ; diarrhœa.
W., æt. 29, well built, choleric-phlegmatic temperament, accustomed to much traveling ; headache.
Woman, æt. 30, abortion at fourth month, followed by suppression of lochia.
Girl, æt. 30, tall, slender and healthy, although somewhat pale and emaciated in consequence of former abdominal troubles.
Woman, wife of an apothecary, suffered for fourteen months under unsuccessful allopathic treatment ; chronic morning diarrhœa.
Girl, æt. 33, lively disposition ; colic before appearance of menses.
Man, æt. 34, suffering for eight days from periodical recurrence of pain in right eye ; rheumatic inflammation of eye.
Mrs. ---, æt. 37, in consequence of taking cold ; peritonitis.
Man, æt. 38 ; colic from vexation.
Mrs. C. E. H., æt. about 38, always been in good health, married ten years ; never pregnant ; ovarian tumor.
Man, æt. 40, after catching cold and heavy lifting ; coxalgia.
Potter, æt. 40, had rheumatism and lead colic, suffering all Winter and Spring ; lumbago.
Mrs. ---, a lady, æt. about 40, had been for two or three years suffering from chronic diarrhœa, nervous prostration and general debility ; the result of mental overexertion.
Military man, æt. 40, suffering for nine months ; allopathic treatment without result ; coxalgia.
Woman, æt. 44, mild disposition, short in build ; after having fallen twice ; inflammation about the abdomen.
PL., æt. 55, always been in good health until within four or five years, since when he has been suffering from piles ; ischias.
Woman, æt. 56, suffering from gastralgia and gout, followed by inflammation of eyes ; choleric temperament, venous, hemorrhoidal constitution ; choroiditis.
Man, æt. 56, sanguine-choleric temperament, has been suffering for twenty years from attacks of colic.
Man, æt. 59, active ; sciatica.
Man, æt. 60, otherwise healthy ; faceache.
The wife of a custom clerk, æt. 64, had suffered for two years ; ischias.
Woman, æt. 78, subject to attacks of vertigo for one year, otherwise healthy ; dysentery.
   

RELATIONS. [48] [Coloc.]
Antidoted by : Camphor., Caustic., Chamom., Coffea, Opium, Staphis.
Large doses are counteracted by tepid milk, infusion of galls, Camphor. and Opium.
It antidotes : Caustic., Magnes.
Compatible : Coloc. in alternation with Staphis. cured ovarian pains ; after Chamom. in abdominal pains and first stage of cholera.
Complementary : Mercur. in dysentery with much tenesmus.
Compare : Act. rac., Arnic., Bellad., Bryon. (closed analogue), Canthar., Caustic., Chamom., Chelid., Cinchon., (beer intoxicates easily), Coccul., Coffea, Digit., Gambog., Lycop., Mercur., Nux vom., Plumbum (inclination to assume strange attitudes in bed), Pulsat., Staphis. (anger with vexation, abdominal pains, neuralgia, etc.), Veratr.
